scope: Read-only source review of three-path physical access-path fix. No product execution, new Cargo build, workflow mutation or task completion.

Deleting each document_manifest parent probes child chunk_symbol_identity by doc_key; existing child primary key(chunk_id) and index(file_path) do not provide this equality access path.

A D-document deletion in I identity rows can execute Theta(D*I) child scanning without the new index; the non-unique B-tree doc_key index changes that child access to indexed lookup. Actual end-to-end speedup remains unmeasured here.
semantics: Fresh FULL_SCHEMA_SQL installs the new non-unique index without altering tables, columns, constraints, triggers or stored representation.

Existing current schema 25 runs CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on ordinary writable open, after the existing semantic_outbox index maintenance; no row rewrite, schema-version bump or direct epoch/incarnation mutation.
Existing version!=0 and !=25 returns Mismatch before the index-creation branch; historical v21/v24 rebuild contracts remain unchanged.
DDL failures propagate through db_err and ?, not fallback reset; query_only remains enabled and rejects a missing-index installation.
Full staging and direct writer derive drop/recreate index lists from FULL_SCHEMA_SQL; the new access path is restored as part of the existing protocol.
No modification to resolution frontier, durable recovery, budgets, closure completion, 15-table oracle or raw sampling/host strata.
test_review: Existing four schema-guard tests are retained; fresh-schema control now requires the index and parent-delete EXPLAIN SEARCH.

New test constructs current-schema rows, drops the index, requires original child SCAN, records every SQL table and metadata, requires query_only refusal, reopens twice and requires identical rows plus indexed SEARCH.
Actual parent deletion retains only the intended other child row and PRAGMA foreign_key_check is empty.
compatibility_with_prefix_window_833: Disjoint 3 cc-db paths vs single cc-index reconcile.rs path; no changes to the witness theorem, same-prepare lifetime, epoch fence or actual SqlWork accounting.
limitations: First writable open of a large existing DB pays real index-build time/space/lock cost; existing busy/disk errors must remain visible.
Index maintenance adds storage and insertion costs; end-to-end scale performance requires source-bound execution.
This index does not eliminate repeated dependency-prefix SQL or full scan per resume, and cannot alone justify attributing old fresh-staging or oracle time to child-key deletion.
